mainTopic: Trustworthiness and acceptance as a חבר or גר: how suspicion spreads, full acceptance, and the procedure for becoming a חבר
overview: The amud opens by finishing a מחלוקת about who the חכמים of the משנה are. One view says רבי יהודה, and the other says רבי מאיר, who holds that a חבר suspected on one matter is suspected on the whole Torah. A גר suspected on one matter is treated like a ישראל משומד, but his קידושין are still valid. A ברייתא rules that a would-be חבר, a גר, a לוי, or a כהן who rejects even one detail is not accepted, and a פסוק is brought for the כהן. The גמרא then lays out how someone becomes a חבר: whether he is taught before or after acceptance, starting with purity of the hands, and how long the trial period lasts. The text of בית הלל's view is corrected to thirty days for both liquids and clothing. After a סימן listing the coming topics, ברייתות discuss accepting חבר status before three חברים, and whether the household or a תלמיד חכם must also do so. The story of the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס shows that כהנים, after the חורבן, did not entrust טהרות to anyone. The amud ends with the status of a deceased חבר's family, and of people who move into or out of a חבר's household, where רבי מאיר requires a new acceptance and supports it with a story.

steps.title: First view: the Sages of the משנה are רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The first אמורא finishes his statement: one suspected on שביעית is suspected on מעשר, and the חכמים of the משנה are רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: [One suspected on שביעית] is suspected on מעשר. And who are the חכמים? רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the first אמורא's opinion, which started earlier. He says that suspicion on שביעית carries over to מעשר, and he identifies the חכמים of the משנה as רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהודה's area, people treated שביעית as very serious. So if a person is willing to break שביעית, the stricter matter, he would surely break מעשר, the lighter one. This view does not say suspicion spreads to everything. It only spreads from a strict matter down to a lighter one.

keyTerms.meaning: Suspected; a person we cannot trust on a certain halacha
Tithes that must be separated from produce
And who are the 'Sages' mentioned in the משנה?

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words 'suspected on מעשר' are the end of the first אמורא's statement, whose opening appeared earlier.

phrases.english: is suspected regarding tithes,
phrases.notes: End of the first opinion: one suspected on שביעית is suspected on מעשר.

phrases.english: And who are 'the Sages'? Rabbi Yehuda,
phrases.notes: In his locale שביעית was treated stringently.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן חֲכָמִים? רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first אמורא's explanation begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, suspicion on the strict matter (שביעית) extends to the lighter matter (מעשר).

steps.title: Second view: the Sages of the משנה are רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The second אמורא says that one suspected on מעשר is also suspected on שביעית, and the חכמים are רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one says: one suspected on מעשר is suspected on שביעית. And who are the חכמים? רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The other אמורא gives the opposite direction: even suspicion on the lighter matter (מעשר) spreads to שביעית. He says the חכמים of the משנה are רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This view does not ask which matter is stricter. Following רבי מאיר, once someone is suspected on one thing, we suspect him on others too. The גמרא will now bring a ברייתא to show that this is really רבי מאיר's position.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one says (the second of two disputing אמוראים)
The seventh (Sabbatical) year and the laws of its produce

phrases.english: And the other one says:

phrases.aramaic: הֶחָשׁוּד עַל הַמַּעֲשֵׂר חָשׁוּד עַל הַשְּׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: One suspected regarding tithes is suspected regarding the Sabbatical Year,
And who are 'the Sages'? Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחַד אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing explanation of who the חכמים are.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, suspicion spreads even from מעשר to שביעית.

steps.title: Proof: רבי מאיר holds suspicion on one matter spreads to everything
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי מאיר's view: a חבר suspected on one matter is suspected on the whole Torah. The חכמים say only on that one matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: an עם הארץ who took on the commitments of a חבר and was then suspected on one matter is suspected on the whole Torah. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say he is suspected only on that matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the claim that רבי מאיר believes suspicion spreads. It shows that the second אמורא's view fits רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, one proven lapse breaks the person's whole trustworthiness. The חכמים in this ברייתא disagree and limit the suspicion to the one area where he failed. That is why, for the second אמורא, suspicion on מעשר reaching שביעית must come from רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא (introduces a supporting source)
A person not careful about טומאה and מעשרות
The commitments of a חבר (care with tithes and purity)
Becomes suspected regarding the entire Torah

phrases.english: As it is taught: an am ha'aretz
who accepted upon himself the commitments of a chaver,
and was then suspected regarding one matter —
he is suspected regarding the entire Torah,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ נֶחְשָׁד אֶלָּא לְאוֹתוֹ דָּבָר בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: He is suspected only regarding that particular matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second אמורא's identification of the חכמים as רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי מאיר holds suspicion on one matter spreads to other matters.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא דמאי) about a חבר who was suspected on one matter.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: suspected on one thing means suspected on everything. חכמים: suspected only on that one thing.

steps.title: A convert suspected on one matter is like a Jewish transgressor
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a גר suspected on one matter is suspected on the whole Torah and is treated like a ישראל משומד.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גר who accepted the Torah, even if he was suspected on one matter, is suspected on the whole Torah and is like a ישראל משומד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא, this time about a convert. It rules that if he fails in one area, he is suspected on everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the ruling is stated with no dispute. Even one lapse makes the גר suspect on the whole Torah. The ברייתא adds that his status becomes like a Jew who habitually sins.

keyTerms.meaning: All the מצוות of the Torah
A Jew who habitually transgresses מצוות

phrases.english: A convert who accepted upon himself the words of Torah,
even if he was suspected regarding one matter —
he is suspected regarding the entire Torah,
and he is like a Jewish transgressor.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַגֵּר שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same topic of spreading suspicion with a second ברייתא, about a גר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר suspected on one matter is suspected on all, and has the status of a ישראל משומד.

steps.title: Practical result: his betrothal is still valid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why it matters that he is like a ישראל משומד: if he betroths a woman, his קידושין are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: The practical difference: if he betroths, his betrothal is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the practical point of calling him 'like a ישראל משומד'. Even as a sinner, he is still Jewish, so his קידושין work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think a גר who abandons מצוות goes back to being a non-Jew. The comparison to a ישראל משומד teaches that he stays Jewish. A Jew's קידושין are valid even when he sins, so his are valid too.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Suspected on the whole Torah' does not cancel his conversion. He has the status of a sinning Jew, not a גוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: A conversion that was properly done cannot be undone by later sinning.

phrases.english: The practical difference is,
that if he betroths a woman — his betrothal is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical result of the 'ישראל משומד' comparison.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: His status as a Jew remains, so his קידושין take effect.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גר suspected on the whole Torah still has the status of a sinning Jew, so his קידושין are valid.

steps.title: Accepting all but one matter is not accepted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that someone who wants to become a חבר, or a גוי who wants to convert, but rejects even one matter, is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: one who comes to accept the commitments of a חבר except for one matter is not accepted. A גוי who comes to accept the Torah except for one matter is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא moves from people who failed after joining to people who set conditions before joining. Anyone who holds back even one matter is turned away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being a חבר, or becoming a גר, requires full acceptance. Leaving out one item shows the commitment is not complete. This matches the earlier idea that one gap affects the whole.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who comes to accept the commitments of a chaver,
except for one matter —
we do not accept him.
A gentile who comes to accept the words of Torah,
except for one matter —
we do not accept him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from suspicion after acceptance to conditions set at the time of acceptance.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Partial acceptance, missing even one matter, disqualifies a would-be חבר or גר.

steps.title: Even one detail of rabbinic law
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says that even rejecting one fine detail of דברי סופרים is enough to be turned away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: even one fine detail of the words of the Scribes.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה adds to the ברייתא. He says the rule applies even to a small detail of rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might have thought 'one matter' means only a Torah-level law. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה teaches that even a tiny rabbinic detail counts. Rejecting it is still not accepting the full system.
steps.whatToRemember: A חבר or a גר must accept everything. Even one rejected rabbinic detail blocks acceptance.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the classic source that a convert must accept all the מצוות, including rabbinic ones.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
Even one fine detail of the words of the Scribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the rule of the previous ברייתא to rabbinic details.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rejecting even a minor rabbinic detail disqualifies the candidate.

steps.title: A לוי or כהן who rejects one detail is not accepted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the same 'all or nothing' rule applies to a לוי accepting the duties of a לוי and a כהן accepting the duties of כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Likewise, a לוי who comes to accept the duties of a לוי, or a כהן who comes to accept the duties of כהונה, except for one thing, is not accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the previous step keeps going. It adds the לוי and the כהן to the list of people who are turned away if they reject even one item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the rule covered a would-be חבר and a גר. Now it is applied to a person's role within the עבודה. A כהן cannot pick and choose which parts of כהונה he accepts.

keyTerms.meaning: A Levite, a member of the tribe of לוי
The duties and laws that belong to a Levite
The duties and laws that belong to the priesthood

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן בֶּן לֵוִי שֶׁבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי לְוִיָּה,
phrases.english: And similarly, a Levite who comes to accept the matters of a Levite,
and a priest who comes to accept the matters of priesthood,
except for one matter —
he is not accepted,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן בֶּן לֵוִי שֶׁבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי לְוִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the 'reject one thing and you are not accepted' rule from the חבר and גר to the לוי and כהן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לוי or כהן who accepts his duties except for one detail is not accepted.

steps.title: Verse proof: a priest who denies any service has no share in priesthood
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא brings a פסוק about the כהן who offers the blood and fat of the שלמים. It teaches that a כהן who denies any part of the עבודה loses his share in כהונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'He who offers the blood of the peace offerings, and the fat, among the sons of אהרן, shall have the right thigh as a portion.' This means that any כהן who does not accept the service given to the sons of אהרן has no portion in כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a source from the תורה for the rule in the previous step about the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the portion goes to the one 'who offers' among the sons of אהרן. This is read to mean that only a כהן who accepts the עבודה receives a share. If he denies even one part of it, he does not count as a full member of כהונה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He who offers the blood of the peace offerings' (ויקרא ז:לג)
The service that was handed over (to the כהנים)

steps.whyThisMatters: It gives a פסוק as a model for the whole 'all or nothing' principle: belonging to a group depends on accepting all of its obligations.

phrases.english: as it is stated: 'He who sacrifices the blood of the peace offerings, etc.',
phrases.notes: ויקרא ז:לג — the end of the verse gives him the right thigh as a portion.

phrases.english: the service which is handed over to the sons of Aaron,
any priest who does not admit to it —
has no share in the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the scriptural source for the כהן rule in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a כהן who rejects one part of כהונה is not accepted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא ז:לג, 'המקריב את דם השלמים... מבני אהרן'.

steps.title: Accept first or teach first: it depends on his private conduct
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: if a would-be חבר is already seen keeping these practices privately at home, he is accepted first and taught afterward. If not, he is taught first and accepted afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: someone who comes to take on the practices of a חבר is handled this way. If we have seen him keep them modestly inside his home, we accept him and then teach him. If not, we teach him and then accept him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the order of acceptance: does the person become a חבר before or after he learns the details?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depends on whether he has already shown commitment in private. If he has, he can be trusted right away and learn the fine points later. If he has not, he must first learn the details, and only then is he accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: The practices of a חבר, someone careful about טהרות and מעשרות

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת,
phrases.english: The Sages taught: One who comes to accept the matters of ḥaver status,

phrases.aramaic: אִם רְאִינוּהוּ שֶׁנּוֹהֵג בְּצִינְעָה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ —
phrases.english: if we have seen that he practices them privately within his home —

phrases.aramaic: מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְלַמְּדִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: he is accepted, and afterward he is taught.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — מְלַמְּדִין אוֹתוֹ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: And if not — he is taught, and afterward he is accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from whether he is accepted at all to the order of accepting and teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If he already practices privately, he is accepted and then taught. Otherwise he is taught and then accepted.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחי: always accept first
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי disagrees. Either way, the person is accepted first and keeps learning as he goes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוחי says: in either case we accept him, and he keeps learning in the normal way.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion inside the same ברייתא argues with the first view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view makes acceptance depend on his past private conduct. רבי שמעון בן יוחי does not make that distinction. He holds that a sincere commitment is enough to accept him, and he will pick up the details over time, the way every חבר learns.
steps.whatToRemember: First view: past private practice decides the order. רבי שמעון בן יוחי: always accept first and let him learn along the way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ,
phrases.english: whether this way or that way, he is accepted,
and he continues to learn in the usual manner.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the first view in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: He is always accepted first and learns the details as he goes.

steps.title: Acceptance starts with purity of the hands
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a would-be חבר is first accepted for the purity of his hands, and afterward for טהרות in general. Accepting only the hands is allowed. Accepting טהרות without the hands is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: we accept him first for the hands (washing them before touching pure things), and afterward for purity in general. If he says, 'I accept only the hands,' we accept him. If he accepts general purity but not the hands, then he has not really accepted general purity either.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא lays out the steps of becoming a חבר. Hand-washing comes first, and the broader purity laws come after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hand purity is the easiest and most basic step, so it can be taken on alone. Someone who claims to accept the harder general purity laws while refusing the easy hand-washing shows that his commitment is not real. So even his acceptance of טהרות is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'wings'; here it means hands, i.e., the purity of one's hands
Ritual purity in general, especially of food

steps.confusionAlert: כנפים here does not mean the corners of a garment (ציצית). It is a borrowed word for the hands.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: He is accepted first for hands,
and afterward he is accepted for purity,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אָמַר: ״אֵינִי מְקַבֵּל אֶלָּא לִכְנָפַיִם״ — מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ.
phrases.english: and if he said: 'I accept only for hands' — he is accepted.
If he accepted for purity but did not accept for hands —
he has not been accepted even for purity.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מְקַבְּלִין לִכְנָפַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the procedure for becoming a חבר, now describing the order of the commitments themselves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hand purity comes first and may be accepted alone. Accepting טהרות without hand purity is not valid.

steps.title: How long until he is fully accepted?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא asks how long the trial period lasts before the would-be חבר is trusted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: for how long [must he prove himself] before we accept him?
steps.whatsHappening: This ברייתא opens with a question. It is setting up the dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we learned how and in what order he is accepted. Now the question is about time: how long must he keep these practices before he is fully trusted?

keyTerms.meaning: Until how much, for how long

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַד כַּמָּה מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ?
phrases.english: The Sages taught: Until when is he accepted?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: עַד כַּמָּה מְקַבְּלִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the question of a time period to the acceptance process.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length of the trial period before he is considered a trustworthy חבר.

steps.title: Thirty days or twelve months: בית שמאי and בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי say thirty days for liquids and twelve months for clothing. בית הלל say twelve months for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: for liquids, thirty days; for clothing, twelve months. בית הלל say: for both, twelve months.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי treat the purity of liquids as something learned quickly, so thirty days is enough, while the purity of clothing needs a full year. בית הלל make no distinction: both areas require a twelve-month trial.
steps.whatToRemember: To become a חבר, he must accept every detail, start with the hands, and pass a trial period. The length of that period is disputed between בית שמאי and בית הלל. The next two steps show that the version of בית הלל given here is challenged and corrected to thirty days for both.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
for liquids — thirty days,
for clothing — twelve months.
And Beit Hillel say:

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה — לִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: both this and that — for twelve months.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בית שמאי: thirty days for liquids and twelve months for clothing. בית הלל: twelve months for both.

steps.title: Problem: this would make בית הלל stricter than בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the ruling as recorded would be a case where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this would be one of the cases where בית שמאי are lenient and בית הלל are strict.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the version of the ברייתא from Step 14. As written, it makes בית הלל (twelve months for both) stricter than בית שמאי (thirty days for liquids).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cases where בית שמאי are more lenient than בית הלל are rare. They are all collected in מסכת עדיות, and this case is not on that list. So the recorded version must be wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem that follows from what was just said

steps.confusionAlert: The source itself does not mention עדיות. The point is that the known list of 'בית שמאי lenient, בית הלל strict' cases (found in עדיות) does not include this one.

phrases.english: If so,
this would be among the leniencies of Beit Shammai
and among the stringencies of Beit Hillel,
phrases.notes: Such cases are listed in עדיות, and this one is not there.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, הָוֵה לֵיהּ מִקּוּלֵּי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּמֵחוּמְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of בית הלל's view in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The recorded version of בית הלל: twelve months for both liquids and clothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That version makes בית הלל stricter than בית שמאי. Yet this case is missing from the known list of such cases, so the version cannot be correct.

steps.title: Corrected text: בית הלל say thirty days for both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the ברייתא: בית הלל require thirty days for both liquids and clothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, בית הלל say: both this and that require thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by changing the text of בית הלל's opinion. בית הלל say thirty days for both liquids and clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now בית הלל are more lenient on clothing (thirty days instead of twelve months) and equal on liquids. So this is no longer a case of בית הלל being stricter, and the קשיא disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this and that (here: liquids and clothing)

steps.whatToRemember: Final version: בית שמאי say thirty days for liquids and twelve months for clothing. בית הלל say thirty days for both.

phrases.english: Rather, Beit Hillel say:
Both this and that (liquids and clothing) are thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 15 by correcting the text.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Text correction: the ברייתא is reworded.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל require twelve months for both.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל require thirty days for both, so they are not stricter than בית שמאי.

steps.title: Memory aid for the topics ahead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a mnemonic listing the upcoming subjects.
steps.simpleTranslation: Mnemonic: חבר, student, תכלת, tax, returned, tax collector, by himself.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. The גמרא gives a list of key words to help us remember the topics coming up until the end of the פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to an upcoming ברייתא. For example, 'חבר' points to the next ברייתא and 'תלמיד' to the one after it. It works like a table of contents.

phrases.english: (Mnemonic: haver, student, sky-blue dye,
tax, returned, tax collector, by himself).

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Editorial mnemonic (not a true argumentative step)
steps.triggerLanguage: סִימָן: חָבֵר, תַּלְמִיד, תְּכֵלֶת, מֶכֶס, חָזַר, גַּבַּאי, בְּעַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition that sets up the new series of ברייתות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is a list of upcoming topics.

steps.title: Acceptance must be before three חברים, but not for the household
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: a would-be חבר must accept in front of three חברים, but his children and household do not need to.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who comes to take on the practices of a חבר must accept them in front of three חברים. His children and household do not need to accept in front of three חברים.
steps.whatsHappening: A new ברייתא teaches how a person becomes a חבר: by formally accepting in front of three existing חברים. His family is covered by his acceptance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds a new requirement: a public, formal acceptance before three. The תנא קמא holds that the family members are included through the head of the house and need no separate ceremony.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: introduces a ברייתא
The practices of a חבר (careful about טהרות and מעשרות)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who comes to accept the practices of a haver
must accept in the presence of three haverim,
but his children and household members

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָן צְרִיכִין לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים.
phrases.english: do not need to accept in the presence of three haverim.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the first topic named in the סימן ('חבר').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Acceptance of חבר status requires three חברים. The family is included without its own acceptance.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: the household must accept too
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds that the children and household also need their own acceptance before three, because a son of a חבר is not like a חבר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Even his children and household must accept in front of three חברים, because a חבר who accepted is not the same as the son of a חבר who accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the first opinion. He requires the family to make their own formal acceptance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His reason is that the father personally committed in front of three. The son only 'accepted' by being part of his father's home. That is weaker, so the son needs his own acceptance.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even his children and household members
must accept in the presence of three haverim,
because a haver who accepted is not comparable
to the son of a haver who accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא of Step 18 about the household.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The children and household need their own acceptance before three חברים.

steps.title: Even a תלמיד חכם must accept, but a זקן in the ישיבה need not
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא: even a תלמיד חכם must accept before three, but a זקן who sits in the ישיבה is exempt, since he already accepted when he took his seat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who comes to take on the practices of a חבר must accept in front of three חברים, and even a תלמיד חכם must. A זקן who sits in the ישיבה does not need to, because he already accepted from the time he sat there.
steps.whatsHappening: Another ברייתא asks whether Torah scholars are exempt from the formal acceptance. A regular תלמיד חכם is not exempt, but a זקן with a seat in the ישיבה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Knowing the laws is not enough for a regular scholar; he still needs a formal commitment. The זקן is different because taking a seat in the ישיבה already counts as his acceptance.

keyTerms.meaning: An elder who sits in the ישיבה (a recognized senior sage)
From the time he took his seat

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
One who comes to accept the practices of a haver
must accept in the presence of three haverim,
and even a Torah scholar
must accept in the presence of three haverim.
An elder who sits in the yeshiva

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים,
phrases.english: does not need to accept in the presence of three haverim,
because he already accepted it upon himself
from the time he sat (in the yeshiva).

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַבָּא לְקַבֵּל דִּבְרֵי חֲבֵירוּת — צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים, וַאֲפִילּוּ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes up the next סימן word ('תלמיד'): who among scholars is exempt from the acceptance rule of Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם must accept before three. A זקן who sits in the ישיבה is exempt because his sitting counts as acceptance.

steps.title: אבא שאול: a תלמיד חכם is exempt, and others may accept before him
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול holds that even a תלמיד חכם needs no acceptance, and others may even accept חבר status in front of him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: Even a תלמיד חכם does not need to accept in front of three חברים. Not only that, but others may accept in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא שאול disagrees with the previous ברייתא. He gives a תלמיד חכם the same exemption as the זקן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אבא שאול, being a Torah scholar already proves the person's commitment. So the scholar is automatically a חבר. He is trusted enough that new חברים can make their acceptance in front of him.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion
And not only that, but even more
They accept (חבר status) in front of him

steps.whatToRemember: There are two disputes about the formal acceptance before three. The first is about the household (תנא קמא vs. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל). The second is about the תלמיד חכם (תנא קמא vs. אבא שאול). Everyone agrees a זקן in the ישיבה is exempt.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says:
Even a Torah scholar

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ צָרִיךְ לְקַבֵּל בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה חֲבֵירִים,
phrases.english: does not need to accept in the presence of three haverim,
and not only that, but
others may accept (haver status) in his presence.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּא שָׁאוּל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with Step 20 about the תלמיד חכם.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תלמיד חכם is exempt from acceptance, and others may accept חבר status in front of him.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן dates the rule to a specific era
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says this teaching was taught in the days of the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: This teaching was taught in the days of the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן tells us when the rule from Step 20 was taught: that even a תלמיד חכם must accept חבר status before three. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that even a scholar must formally accept seems surprising. רבי יוחנן links it to a specific time, which suggests it came from a period when scholars were not automatically trusted with purity. The next step tells the story that shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: Was taught (it was formulated as a teaching)
This teaching (here, the ברייתא that even a תלמיד חכם must accept)
A תנא who was a כהן

steps.confusionAlert: "מִשְׁנָה זוֹ" here does not mean a משנה in our מסכת. It refers to the ברייתא in Step 20, that even a תלמיד חכם must accept before three.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בִּימֵי בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס
phrases.english: In the days of the son of Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus
this teaching was taught.
phrases.notes: Referring to the rule that even a תלמיד חכם must accept before three.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בִּימֵי בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס נִשְׁנֵית מִשְׁנָה זוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the historical background of the first view in Step 20, against אבא שאול in Step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The requirement that even a תלמיד חכם accept before three dates from the era of the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס.

steps.title: The story of the visiting students and the pure items
steps.stepSummary: Students sent by the Sages find the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס carrying טהרות. He seats his own scholars next to them to guard his items while he looks into their question.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי had a doubt about a matter of purity. The Sages sent people to the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס and told them: go tell him to look into it. They found him carrying pure items. He seated Sages of his own next to them, and he stood up to look into the question.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the story behind רבי יוחנן's statement. The son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס did not trust the visiting scholars around his טהרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He placed his own trusted scholars next to the visitors so they would not touch and contaminate his pure items. That treated the visitors as people not trusted with purity, even though they were scholars. This is the attitude behind the rule that even a תלמיד חכם must formally accept חבר status.

keyTerms.meaning: They had a doubt about a matter
Items kept in a state of ritual purity

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei
were in doubt about a matter of purity,
the Sages sent people to

phrases.aramaic: בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן אַנְטִיגְנוֹס,
phrases.english: the son of Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus,
[saying:] Go tell him to look into it.
phrases.notes: The message for the son to examine the question.

phrases.english: They found him carrying pure items,
he seated Sages of his own next to them,
phrases.notes: To guard his טהרות from the visitors.

phrases.english: and he stood up to look into it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אִיסְתַּפַּק לְהוּ מִילְּתָא בִּטְהָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the story that explains רבי יוחנן's dating.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס treated visiting scholars as not trusted with his טהרות.

steps.title: רבי יהודה protests the insult to scholars
steps.stepSummary: When told what happened, רבי יהודה complains that this man, like his father, disrespects תלמידי חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came and told רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי. רבי יהודה said to them: This man's father insulted Torah scholars, and he too insults Torah scholars!
steps.whatsHappening: The students report back, and רבי יהודה reacts angrily. He sees not trusting scholars as an insult to תלמידי חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, treating scholars as if they were not trustworthy with purity is disrespectful. He says the son follows the same bad pattern as his father. This complaint sets up רבי יוסי's defense in the next step.

phrases.english: They came and told it
to Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Yosei,
Rabbi Yehuda said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אָבִיו שֶׁל זֶה בִּיזָּה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים,
phrases.english: This man's father insulted Torah scholars,
and he too insults Torah scholars!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אָבִיו שֶׁל זֶה בִּיזָּה תַּלְמִידֵי חֲכָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the son's behavior described in Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה views distrust of scholars in purity matters as an insult to תלמידי חכמים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conduct of the son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, who did not trust the visiting scholars with his טהרות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Treating תלמידי חכמים as untrustworthy with purity is disrespectful to them, and the son repeats his father's pattern.

steps.title: רבי יוסי defends the priest's strictness
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says to keep honoring the elder. Since the חורבן, כהנים took on a higher standard and do not hand טהרות to anyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said to him: Let the elder's honor stay in its place. Rather, from the day the Temple was destroyed, the priests took on an extra standard for themselves: they do not hand over pure items to anyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers רבי יהודה's complaint. He explains that the son was not insulting scholars. He was following a strict practice that כהנים adopted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי changes how we read the event. It was not personal disrespect but a general priestly practice that applied to everyone after the חורבן. So the son's behavior was proper, and his honor should not be harmed.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra standard of strictness, refinement

steps.whatToRemember: The son's distrust was not an insult. It reflected a strict standard כהנים took on after the חורבן: not entrusting טהרות to anyone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said to him:
Let the honor of the elder stay in its place,
rather, from the day the Temple was destroyed
priests took on an extra standard for themselves,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין מוֹסְרִין אֶת הַטְּהָרוֹת לְכׇל אָדָם.
phrases.english: that they do not hand pure items to any person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: כְּבוֹד זָקֵן יְהֵא מוּנָּח בִּמְקוֹמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה's complaint in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recasting the behavior: a general priestly practice, not personal disrespect.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The son of רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס was showing contempt for scholars.
steps.terutzMaskana: He was following the post-חורבן priestly practice of not entrusting טהרות to anyone.

steps.title: A deceased חבר's family keeps its trusted status
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: after a חבר dies, his wife, children, and household remain trusted until suspected. Likewise, a courtyard where תכלת is sold stays trusted until it is disqualified.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If a חבר died, his wife, children, and household keep their presumed status until they come under suspicion. Similarly, a courtyard where sky-blue dye is sold keeps its presumed status until it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about how long trusted status lasts. A חבר's family does not lose it just because he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While the חבר was alive, his household was presumed to follow his standards. That presumption (חזקה) continues after his death until there is real reason to suspect them. The same logic applies to a known תכלת seller's courtyard: it stays trusted until something disqualifies it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a general principle: an established חזקה of trustworthiness stays in place until real evidence undermines it.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
A חבר who died —
his wife, his children, and his household members
keep their presumed status until they are suspected.
And similarly, a courtyard where sky-blue dye is sold —
keeps its presumed status until it is disqualified.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חָבֵר שֶׁמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the halachic topic of the חבר's household (Steps 18–19) and discusses how long their status lasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A deceased חבר's household keeps its trusted חזקה until suspected; a תכלת seller's courtyard keeps its חזקה until disqualified.

steps.title: People coming into a חבר's home must accept the rules
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that the wife, daughter, or slave of an עם הארץ who comes into a חבר's household must accept דברי חבירות from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The wife of an עם הארץ who later marries a חבר, and likewise the daughter of an עם הארץ who marries a חבר, and likewise the slave of an עם הארץ who is sold to a חבר — all of them must accept the rules of being a חבר from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It lists three kinds of people who move from an עם הארץ household into a חבר household, and says they must formally accept the rules of חבירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Joining a חבר's household does not make a person trusted automatically. These people grew up with or lived by the looser habits of an עם הארץ. So they must make their own commitment to the rules of purity and מעשרות before they are trusted.

keyTerms.meaning: An unlearned person who is not careful about purity and מעשרות
A person who has formally committed to keep purity and מעשרות carefully
The rules and commitments of being a חבר
From the start; at the outset

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
the wife of an am ha'aretz who married a ḥaver,
phrases.notes: She was formerly married to an עם הארץ and later married a חבר.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְחָבֵר,
phrases.english: and likewise the daughter of an am ha'aretz who married a ḥaver,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן עַבְדּוֹ שֶׁל עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּמְכַּר לְחָבֵר —
phrases.english: and likewise the slave of an am ha'aretz who was sold to a ḥaver —
all of them must accept
the matters of ḥaver status from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵשֶׁת עַם הָאָרֶץ שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְחָבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of step 26, which dealt with a חבר's household staying trusted. Now it asks about people entering or leaving such a household.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone coming from an עם הארץ household into a חבר household must accept דברי חבירות from the start.

steps.title: People leaving a חבר's home do not need to accept again
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the wife, daughter, or slave of a חבר who goes into an עם הארץ's household does not need to accept דברי חבירות again.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the wife of a חבר who later marries an עם הארץ, and likewise the daughter of a חבר who marries an עם הארץ, and likewise the slave of a חבר who is sold to an עם הארץ — they do not need to accept the rules of being a חבר from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the reverse case. People who come from a חבר's home do not need a new acceptance, even after moving into an עם הארץ's home.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people already lived by the rules of חבירות. They keep that trusted status even though their new household is not careful. The first opinion assumes good habits stay with a person.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the reverse direction. Here the person comes FROM a חבר's home and goes INTO an עם הארץ's home. Do not mix this up with the case in step 27.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵשֶׁת חָבֵר שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְעַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: But the wife of a ḥaver who married an am ha'aretz,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן בִּתּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְעַם הָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: and likewise the daughter of a ḥaver who married an am ha'aretz,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן עַבְדּוֹ שֶׁל חָבֵר שֶׁנִּמְכַּר לְעַם הָאָרֶץ —
phrases.english: and likewise the slave of a ḥaver who was sold to an am ha'aretz —
they do not need to accept
the matters of ḥaver status from the start.
phrases.notes: They are already used to acting as a חבר.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Second half of the same ברייתא as step 27
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אֵשֶׁת חָבֵר שֶׁנִּשֵּׂאת לְעַם הָאָרֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting reverse case to step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those coming from a חבר's household into an עם הארץ's household keep their status without a new acceptance (first opinion).

steps.title: רבי מאיר says they too must accept
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר disagrees with the second case. Even people leaving a חבר's home for an עם הארץ's home must accept דברי חבירות again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: They too must accept upon themselves the rules of being a חבר from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר argues on the second half of the ברייתא. He says even people from a חבר's home must make a new commitment once they live with an עם הארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion trusted that old good habits would last. רבי מאיר worries that a new household changes a person. So he requires a fresh acceptance.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start; at the outset

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
they too must accept upon themselves
the matters of ḥaver status from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף הֵן צְרִיכִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion on the ruling in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even those moving from a חבר's household to an עם הארץ's household must accept דברי חבירות anew.

steps.title: A story of a woman who followed each husband's ways
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, quoting רבי מאיר, tells of a woman who tied תפילין on her first husband, a חבר. When she married an עם הארץ, she tied tax-collector knots on his hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says in the name of רבי מאיר: There was a story with a woman who married a חבר, and she would tie תפילין on his hand for him. She then married an עם הארץ, and she would tie tax-collector's knots on his hand for him.
steps.whatsHappening: A story is brought to support רבי מאיר's view. It shows that a person's behavior changes to match the household they join.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same woman helped her pious husband with a מצוה. Later she helped her second husband with the marks of a tax collector. This shows that past good habits cannot be relied on, which is exactly why רבי מאיר requires a new acceptance.

keyTerms.meaning: Tax-collector's knots or seals worn on the hand

steps.whatToRemember: The first opinion holds that someone from a חבר's home keeps that status. רבי מאיר says a new household can change a person, so everyone must accept דברי חבירות anew. The story of the woman who copied each husband supports רבי מאיר.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a basic principle behind רבי מאיר's view: a person's environment strongly shapes how careful they are. Because of that, trust has to be re-established when someone moves into a new setting.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of Rabbi Meir:
There was an incident with a certain woman who married a ḥaver

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיְתָה קוֹמַעַת לוֹ תְּפִילִּין עַל יָדוֹ,
phrases.english: and she would tie phylacteries on his hand for him,
she then married an am ha'aretz
phrases.notes: Some versions (and the Sefaria translation) read a tax collector here.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיְתָה קוֹשֶׁרֶת לוֹ קִשְׁרֵי מוֹכֵס עַל יָדוֹ.
phrases.english: and she would tie tax-collector's knots on his hand for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּאִשָּׁה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי מאיר's opinion from step 29 with a real-life story.
steps.raayaObject: רבי מאיר's view that even those leaving a חבר's home must accept דברי חבירות anew.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story of a woman whose behavior changed completely to match each husband.
